newsitem.title: ITALY: IMI H1 net profit rises to 276 bln lire.
newsitem.headline: IMI H1 net profit rises to 276 bln lire.

text.p: Net profits at IMI SpA rose to 276 billion lire in the first half of 1997, up some 16 percent from 239 billion lire in the same period last year, the merchant bank said in a statement on Tuesday.

At a group level, the bank said it expected a reasonable increase in profits in the first six months of 1997, but added that, in percentage terms, it would not post as strong growth as the parent company. It gave no group figures.
IMI SpA said loans totalled 46.41 trillion lire by the end of June, up 4.9 percent on June 30, 1996 and up 2.1 percent on December 31, 1996.
IMI said full first half results would be discussed at a board meeting in September.

The statement added that the IMI board had agreed to release up to 200 billion lire of funds to be used to help Banca Popolare di Verona (BPV) acquire 56.8 percent of Credito Bergamasco (Creberg) from France's Credit Lyonnais.
BPV announced earlier this month that it was taking the majority stake in Creberg and added it would then launch a public bid for the bank's remaining capital.
IMI said it would also help BPV with the public bid offer for the remaining Creberg stock, but gave no further details.
